notes: Read all 887 numbered source lines before editing. This is a non-visual API-resilience utility: no JSX, no Recharts/Leaflet/react-leaflet/lucide, no old web-UI components, no i18n strings, and no unit-suffixed (Mi/Min/Mph/Kwh/Kw/Psi) fields. Every API path is preserved verbatim — the fetch URL '${getApiBase()}/api/v1${path}' (L690), the CORS-probe '/api/v1/system/version' HEAD (L812), the /auth/session loop-guard (L258), and fetchSystemStatus('/system/status') (L885). All 20 public exports are reproduced identically: camelCaseKeys, getApiBase, getConnectionStatus, onStatusChange, getReauthUrl, navigateToReauth, _resetAuthExpiredLatch, ApiError, TeslaAuthExpiredError, RateLimitError, UpstreamUnavailableError, pathScope, _resetRateLimitCache, isApiError, isTeslaAuthExpiredError, isRateLimitError, isUpstreamUnavailableError, resilientFetch, SystemStatus, fetchSystemStatus.

L1-8 module JSDoc ported verbatim, then a native-port header documenting every browser-boundary adaptation. The module has ZERO imports (matching the source), so it compiles under Hermes (React Native) and behaves identically under react-native-web where the real window/document/navigator/sessionStorage/fetch exist. Browser boundaries are crossed via globalThis accessors — the established native idiom (columnOrderStore.ts -> globalThis.localStorage, errorReporter.ts -> globalThis.fetch/.location/.navigator).

L10 RequestStatus type and L12-34 snakeToCamel + camelCaseKeys ported byte-for-byte (Array.isArray recursion, Date guard, snake+camel dual-key emission). The replace callback signature matches the proven-clean sibling api/client.ts form `(_, c: string) => c.toUpperCase()` so no-unused-vars stays satisfied.

L36-47 getApiBase: the web `declare global { interface Window { __TESLASYNC_API_BASE__ } }` + `window.__TESLASYNC_API_BASE__` becomes getWindowLike()?.__TESLASYNC_API_BASE__ (typed via a local WindowLike interface; the declare-global is dropped because RN has no lib.dom Window to augment). The `|| ''` fallback to relative paths and the trailing-slash strip are preserved verbatim — absent under Hermes it yields '' exactly as the web build does when nginx injected nothing.

L49-70 offline detection: `_status = navigator.onLine ? 'online':'offline'` -> getNavigatorOnLine() === false ? 'offline':'online' (absent navigator stays online, never blocking). The two `window.addEventListener('online'|'offline')` registrations (L60-61) become optional-chained _statusWindow?.addEventListener?.(...) calls that no-op under Hermes — same effect as the web `typeof window` guard. setStatus, getConnectionStatus, and onStatusChange (with its unsubscribe closure) are ported verbatim.

L72-82 dedup map (inflight Map<string,Promise<unknown>>, get-or-run, finally-delete) ported byte-for-byte. L84-131 reauth section: comments preserved verbatim; DEFAULT_REAUTH_URL '/outpost.goauthentik.io/start' and RETURN_URL_KEY 'teslasync-return-url' constants kept; getReauthUrl reads window.__TESLASYNC_REAUTH_URL__ via getWindowLike() with the same string/trim/empty-string-disables logic.

L133-159 navigateToReauth: sessionStorage.setItem -> getSessionStorage()?.setItem inside the identical best-effort try/catch; window.location.href/.assign/.reload -> getWindowLike()?.location?.* optional calls (href guarded so setItem never receives undefined). Under Hermes the IdP handoff degrades to a no-op (no top-level browser window) — the documented native 'explicit unavailable state'; under react-native-web it is byte-equivalent. The rd= return-destination param construction (encodeURIComponent + ?/& separator) is preserved.

L161-207 auth-expired latch: the _authExpiredHandled boolean, _authExpiredTimer (ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>), resetAuthExpiredLatch, the _resetAuthExpiredLatch test hook, the focus-listener registration (window.addEventListener('focus',...) -> _focusWindow?.addEventListener?.('focus',...)), and handleAuthExpired (latch + 30_000ms timeout + navigateToReauth) are all ported verbatim with every comment, including the auth_session_handler.go 200-on-unauth rationale.

L209-260 Tesla/session expiry events: dispatchTeslaAuthExpired, dispatchSessionExpired, and maybeDispatchSessionExpired (with the /auth/session normalise-and-skip loop-guard) are preserved. The repeated `typeof document === 'undefined'` + `new CustomEvent` boundary is consolidated into one native-safe dispatchDomEvent(type, detail?) that resolves globalThis.document + globalThis.CustomEvent and no-ops when either is absent (Hermes) — behavior-equivalent because the web banner components consuming these events do not exist in the native tree. Event names 'teslasync:tesla-auth-expired' and 'teslasync:session-expired' are kept verbatim.

The two empty cleanup closures use `() => undefined` (sibling api/client.ts convention) to satisfy no-empty-function. The three `controller.abort(reason)` call sites (combineSignals L759/L764 + the _doFetch timeout L823) are routed through a new abortWithReason() helper that casts RN's zero-arg AbortController.abort type to `(r?: unknown) => void`; this fixed the only 3 typecheck errors (TS2554) while still propagating the timeout/user-cancel reason at runtime where the runtime supports it (react-native-web, modern Hermes).

L642-861 _doFetch ported faithfully: rawSignal pulled out and coerced (?? undefined), the cached-RateLimitError short-circuit, the per-attempt userSignal.aborted bailouts, the navigator.onLine offline throw (-> getNavigatorOnLine()===false), per-attempt AbortController+timeout, the fetch with merged signal, setStatus('online'), the HTML-redirect and non-JSON-401 ForwardAuth detection -> maybeDispatchSessionExpired + handleAuthExpired, the structured-error branch (TESLA_TOKEN_EXPIRED -> TeslaAuthExpiredError; plain 401 -> session-expired; 429 -> markRateLimited+RateLimitError; 503 UPSTREAM_BREAKER_OPEN -> UpstreamUnavailableError), camelCaseKeys(await res.json()) on success, the user-cancel-vs-timeout catch, the TypeError CORS auth-probe, the 408 timeout conversion, the jittered exponential backoff (retryDelay*2^attempt*(0.75+random*0.5)) via abortableSleep, and the finally cleanup. The four `new DOMException('aborted','AbortError')` are replaced with makeAbortError() (Error with name='AbortError'; sibling api/client.ts uses the same helper because Hermes historically lacks a DOMException constructor) — abort detection keys off `name`, so behavior is preserved.

L719-722 the untyped `await res.json()` error body is typed as Record<string,unknown> and `new ApiError(err.error || ...)` is rewritten as `typeof errBody.error === 'string' && errBody.error ? errBody.error : `HTTP ${status}`` to keep strict-mode type-safety (unknown cannot be passed where string is expected); the backend `error` field is always a string so this is behavior-equivalent. errBody.code and errBody.upstream use the same typeof-string guards the source already used.
